info.title: Saker Watch API
info.description: Personal stock watchlist and research assistant. Signals are research aids, never financial advice.

get.description: Returns the profile of the authenticated caller. The account is created on the first authenticated request.

put.description: Sets the preferred UI locale and returns the updated profile. Requires an Idempotency-Key: repeating the request with the same key and body replays the first response (Idempotent-Replayed: true); the same key with a different body is rejected with 422.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated key (16-64 letters, digits, '-' or '_') that makes the request safe to retry. A repeat with the same key and body replays the first response.

get.summary: Search stocks to add to the watchlist
get.description: Finds stocks in the enabled markets by ticker or name, an exact ticker first. The market in each match is the canonical one to use in the watchlist routes. Searches are limited per user and, together, per minute and per day; a busy answer carries Retry-After. This is a research aid, not a recommendation.

The caller's stocks with the newest price, how current it is (priceStatus, and staleSince when the last known price is shown) and the performance windows 1D, 1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y and 5Y, computed from adjusted closes in the stock's own currency; a window without enough history carries a reason instead of a number. Filter by market, assetType, q (ticker or name), priceStatus and portfolio (the id of one of the caller's portfolios; 404 when it is not one of theirs); sort by ticker, name, market, createdAt, price or a window (a missing value sorts last); page with limit (1 to 100, default 50) and offset. The answer carries an ETag: send it back in If-None-Match to get 304 when nothing changed. Informational only, not financial advice.

put.summary: Put a stock on the watchlist
put.description: Adds the stock to the caller's watchlist with these notes and target price, or replaces the notes and target of the item already there: the same request twice leaves the same state, so it needs no Idempotency-Key. A stock the catalog does not have yet is registered from the provider's answer for that exact market and ticker and its history is queued; if the provider cannot confirm it the answer is 503 and nothing is stored. Returns 201 when the stock was added and 200 when an item was updated. Because a new stock can spend a provider search, the route shares the stricter per-user limit of the search; a busy answer carries Retry-After.

delete.summary: Take a stock off the watchlist
delete.description: Removes the stock from the caller's watchlist and from every portfolio it was in. Removing a stock that is not there is not an error: the answer is 204 either way.

post.description: Creates a named group of the caller's watchlist stocks, at the end of the list. Names are unique per caller ignoring letter case and spaces at the ends are removed; a caller keeps at most 20 portfolios. Requires an Idempotency-Key: repeating the request with the same key and body replays the first response.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated key (16-64 letters, digits, '-' or '_') that makes the request safe to retry. A repeat with the same key and body replays the first response.

get.description: The caller's portfolios by position, each with the number of stocks it holds. Carries an ETag; send it back in If-None-Match to get 304 when nothing changed.

put.description: Puts the caller's portfolios in the order given, which must name each of them exactly once. The same request twice leaves the same order.

get.description: The portfolio with its stocks by position. Carries an ETag.

put.description: Replaces the name and the description. A name another portfolio of the caller has (ignoring letter case) is a 409. The same request twice leaves the same state.

delete.description: Deletes the portfolio. When stocks would be left in no portfolio they leave the watchlist as well, so the request must carry confirm=true; without it the answer is 409 and nothing changes (see the deletion preview). A portfolio that is already gone is not an error: the answer is 204.

get.description: The group's equal-weighted average and median change over 1D, 1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y and 5Y, with how many stocks have a number for each window and the stock that rose most and least, plus how many stocks have current, stale, pending or unavailable prices. A stock without a number for a window is left out of that window, never counted as zero. A portfolio holds no quantities, so these say how the stocks moved, not how a sum of money did. Informational only, not financial advice. Carries an ETag.

get.summary: See what deleting a portfolio would remove
get.description: Lists the stocks that are in this portfolio and in no other: deleting the portfolio takes them off the watchlist too, with their notes and target prices. Stocks another portfolio also holds stay and are only counted.

put.summary: Put a watchlist stock in a portfolio
put.description: Puts a stock the caller already follows in the portfolio, at the end (201 when it was added, 200 when it was there). A stock that is not on the watchlist is a 404: add it to the watchlist first. A portfolio holds at most 100 stocks.

delete.summary: Take a stock out of a portfolio
delete.description: Takes the stock out of the portfolio; it stays on the watchlist. A stock that is not in the portfolio is not an error: the answer is 204.

put.summary: Reorder the stocks of a portfolio
put.description: Puts the stocks of the portfolio in the order given, which must name each of them exactly once. The same request twice leaves the same order.

id.description: Internal user id (UUIDv7), never the identity provider's subject.

displayName.description: Name sent by the identity provider, if any.

email.description: Email sent by the identity provider, if any.

createdAt.description: When the account was first seen (ISO-8601 UTC).

stocksToRemove.description: Stocks in this portfolio and in no other: they would leave the watchlist, with their notes and targets.

stocksKept.description: How many of its stocks would stay because another portfolio holds them too.

PortfolioDeletionPreviewResponse.description: What deleting a portfolio would do to the watchlist.

position.description: Where it sits in the portfolio, from zero.

addedAt.description: When it was put in the portfolio (ISO-8601 UTC).

priceStatuses.description: How many are in each price state.

staleSince.description: The oldest moment a stale price went stale (ISO-8601 UTC), or null when none is.

PortfolioMetricsResponse.description: The aggregate numbers of a portfolio. Informational only, not financial advice.

name.description: Name; spaces at both ends are removed; 1 to 60 characters.

description.description: Description up to 500 characters, or null.

name.description: Name, unique for the caller ignoring letter case.

position.description: Where it sits among the caller's portfolios, from zero.

PortfolioResponse.description: A portfolio: a named group of the caller's watchlist stocks, kept for observation (never holdings).

value.description: The close as traded, in the stock's currency (a decimal string).

isFinal.description: False while the day may still change.

PriceResponse.description: The newest stored bar of a stock.

stale.description: The last known price is shown.

unavailable.description: No price and loading failed for good.

PriceStatusCountsResponse.description: How many stocks of a portfolio have prices in each state.

notes.description: Notes, up to 2000 characters, or null.

targetPrice.description: Target price greater than zero with at most eight decimals, or null.

PutWatchlistItemRequest.description: Body of `PUT /v1/watchlist/items/{market}/{ticker}`. Both fields replace what is stored; leaving one out clears it.

items.description: Every stock of the portfolio, once, in the order wanted.

portfolioIds.description: Every one of the caller's portfolio ids, once, in the order wanted.

name.description: Instrument name as the provider reports it.

StockCandidateResponse.description: A stock found by a search.

change.description: The change as a fraction (a decimal string; `0.0123` is 1.23 %).

StockChangeResponse.description: A stock and its change over a window.

StockKeyRequest.description: A stock named by market and ticker.

items.description: The matches, an exact ticker first.

targetPrice.description: The caller's target price, or null. A note, never an order.

createdAt.description: When the stock was added (ISO-8601 UTC).

updatedAt.description: When the item last changed (ISO-8601 UTC).

priceStatus.description: `current`, `stale` (the last known price is shown), `pending` (no history yet) or `unavailable` (loading failed for good).

price.description: The newest stored bar, or null when there is none.

staleSince.description: When the price went stale (ISO-8601 UTC), only for `stale`.

windows.description: The eight performance windows, in order.

WatchlistEntryResponse.description: A stock on the caller's watchlist as the list shows it.

targetPrice.description: The caller's target price in the stock's currency, or null. A note, never an order.

createdAt.description: When the stock was added (ISO-8601 UTC).

updatedAt.description: When the item last changed (ISO-8601 UTC).

WatchlistItemResponse.description: A stock on the caller's watchlist.

total.description: How many stocks match the filters, in all pages.

WatchlistPageResponse.description: A page of the caller's watchlist.

WatchlistStockResponse.description: The stock a watchlist item points to.

count.description: How many stocks have a change for the window; the other figures are over these only.

average.description: The equal-weighted average change (a decimal string), or null when no stock has data.

median.description: The median change (a decimal string), or null.

best.description: The stock that rose most, or null.

worst.description: The stock that rose least or fell most, or null.

WindowMetricsResponse.description: What a portfolio did over one window, from the stocks that have a number for it.

change.description: The change as a fraction (a decimal string; `0.0123` is 1.23 %), or null when there is a reason.

baselineDate.description: The day of the close the change is measured from, or null.

reason.description: Why there is no change: `no_data`, `insufficient_history`, `history_gap` or `calendar_unavailable`; null when there is one.

WindowResponse.description: One performance window of a stock, from adjusted closes (ADR-0006, ADR-0030).
